numerical_failure.observed_behavior: A DateOffset addition to a datetime64 value whose exact int64 sum equals iNaT silently returns NaT (dtype datetime64[ns]). Promoting a M8[s] array to the offset's finer nanosecond resolution wraps to an unrelated date: 2500-01-01 + DateOffset(nanoseconds=1) gives 1915-06-14 00:25:26.290448385.

numerical_characteristics.dtype: datetime64[ns] (tz-naive and tz-aware UTC arrays exercised; the test parametrizes tz in [None, "UTC"] and the s->ns example uses M8[s] promoted to ns)
numerical_characteristics.precision: nanosecond (ns) and second (s) resolutions; finer-unit promotion from M8[s] to ns is involved
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Values near the int64 boundary: the sum lands exactly on iNaT (the int64 NaT sentinel), e.g. Timestamp(iNaT + 1) + DateOffset(nanoseconds=-1) returns NaT; DatetimeIndex of 2500-01-01 (M8[s]) + DateOffset(nanoseconds=1) wraps to 1915-06-14 00:25:26.290448385
category_specific_evidence: Property violated: an addition whose exact int64 sum fits in range but equals iNaT must raise OverflowError ('Overflow in int64 addition') rather than silently return NaT; the sum iNaT+1 plus offset -1 is valid int64 yet yields NaT
Reproducer 1: pd.Series([Timestamp(iNaT + 1)]) + pd.DateOffset(nanoseconds=-1) gives NaT with dtype datetime64[ns] (sum equals iNaT)

Reproducer 2: pd.DatetimeIndex(np.array(['2500-01-01'], dtype='M8[s]')) + pd.DateOffset(nanoseconds=1) wraps to an unrelated date 1915-06-14 00:25:26.290448385 on the s->ns promotion, violating the expected 2500-01-01 00:00:00.000000001 value
Test test_dt64arr_add_dateoffset_lands_on_nat_sentinel parametrized over kwds {days:1} and {nanoseconds:1} and tz None/UTC, building DatetimeIndex from iNaT + delta._value with dtype M8[ns]
Affected code paths: RelativeDeltaOffset._apply_array (relativedelta branch and timedelta branch) and the tz-aware UTC fast path in DatetimeArray._add_offset, which previously used raw numpy add
Expected behavior per commit: match add_overflowsafe/astype_overflowsafe and the equivalent Timedelta operations, which raise instead of wrapping
Unit promotion: operands cast to the finer of the two resolutions (matching numpy), with overflow-checked cast via astype_overflowsafe
Related issues referenced: GH#66552 (NaT sentinel landing) and GH#64806 (finer-resolution promotion of offset._pd_timedelta)
reproduction_risks: The reproducer outputs in the PR body are shown as commented/abbreviated (ellipsis in DatetimeIndex repr), so exact expected repr strings should not be assumed beyond what is quoted
Behavior of the tz-aware path depends on whether offset._use_relativedelta is False and the UTC fast-path condition being met

The test expects an OverflowError with message 'Overflow in int64 addition' but the full pytest.raises call is truncated in the passage, so the exact exception type/match for the nanoseconds case is only partially visible
Whether the Series-based reproducer (first example) and the DatetimeIndex reproducer behave identically across pandas versions is not stated
